claims.text: Rapid thermal cycling induces differential thermal expansion among the constituent elements of HfNbTaTiZr.
Differential thermal expansion generates internal residual stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
Rapid thermal cycling generates dislocation networks in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally induced residual stresses and dislocation networks govern the alloy's high-temperature creep behavior.
Thermally induced residual stresses and dislocation networks govern the alloy's thermoelastic behavior.
Slow isothermal annealing and slow cooling minimize thermal-mismatch effects and associated defect formation.
Differences in elemental thermal-expansion coefficients create localized thermal stresses during rapid thermal transitions.
Localized thermal stresses produce lattice distortions.
The resulting microstructural defects alter the alloy's creep behavior.
The resulting microstructural defects alter the alloy's temperature-dependent elastic response.
Rapidly thermally cycled samples will have higher residual-stress levels than slowly cooled, isothermally annealed samples.
Rapidly thermally cycled samples will have higher dislocation densities than slowly cooled, isothermally annealed samples.
Rapidly thermally cycled samples will have higher microhardness than slowly cooled, isothermally annealed samples.
Rapidly thermally cycled samples will show altered temperature-dependent elastic-modulus trends relative to slowly cooled, isothermally annealed samples.
Rapidly thermally cycled samples will have higher tensile-creep rates at 1250 °C than slowly cooled, isothermally annealed samples.
The proposed mechanism primarily applies from approximately 600 °C to 1250 °C.
Outside 600–1250 °C, phase stability or other microstructural factors may influence the response.
Prior observations support the proposed general mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mechanism is said to apply primarily at 600–1250 °C, but the proposed elastic-modulus comparison spans 293–1100 K (about 20–827 °C), much of which lies below the stated mechanistic boundary.
